summary: Very deep module. STUN Binding (T0). TURN Allocate 401 with REALM+NONCE (T1 identity namespace leak). Open TURN Allocate + CreatePermission for 169.254.169.254/127.0.0.1/RFC1918 (T2 — proves bidirectional SSRF into internal network, cloud-metadata reach). RFC 3489 legacy, amplification, TURNS TLS posture. Refresh with lifetime=0 to clean up. Missing: no MESSAGE-INTEGRITY relay/crack loop.

findings.title_pattern: TURN Allocate discloses REALM and NONCE without authentication
findings.tier_evidence: Allocate 401 answer contains REALM+NONCE only against a real TURN endpoint; the realm text is often SIP/AD domain — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed REALM into ldap/kerberos/sip/smtp cross-service correlation; module already implies this.

findings.title_pattern: TURN accepts allocations without authentication (open relay)
findings.tier_evidence: Allocate returned 0x0103 Allocate Success (relayed address given) with NO MESSAGE-INTEGRITY — recce holds a real relay allocation. Refresh lifetime=0 sent to release. This is proof-of-exploit: attacker gets free egress + IP laundering.
findings.promotion_notes: Send data through the allocation (SEND indication) to prove real forwarded traffic; use the relayed address to reflect toward a canary listener.
findings.tester_next_step: turnutils_uclient -v -y IP  # or: python3 stun-turn-toolkit / rfc5766-turn-server client to send data via the open relay

findings.title_pattern: TURN allocation permits relay to internal / loopback / cloud-metadata peer
findings.tier_evidence: After open-relay Allocate, CreatePermission for 169.254.169.254 / 127.0.0.1 / 10.0.0.1 was ACCEPTED — RFC 8656 §9 says MUST refuse. Recce holds a proof primitive of bidirectional SSRF.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain: use TURN to hit 169.254.169.254 IMDS and pull STS credentials on cloud-hosted TURN — hands off to cloud_metadata for finish.
findings.tester_next_step: Use TURN SEND indication to relay HTTP GET /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ toward 169.254.169.254; parse returned STS keys via cloud_metadata.

findings.title_pattern: TURN long-term credentials sent cleartext on 3478 with no TURNS (5349) alternative
findings.tier_evidence: Correlation between speaks_turn on 3478 and absence of TURNS on 5349.
findings.promotion_notes: Would need a live capture of a real client's MESSAGE-INTEGRITY hash for offline crack (hashcat -m 31300).
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:5349  # confirms no TURNS; tcpdump -i any 'udp and port 3478' to capture client hashes over time

findings.title_pattern: STUN/TURN SOFTWARE attribute discloses server version
STUN Binding Response reveals scanner's external IP mapping
findings.tier_evidence: XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS is the design of STUN Binding.

findings.title_pattern: STUN server responds to legacy RFC 3489 ClassicSTUN
findings.tier_evidence: Posture — a legacy request-parse acceptance flag.
findings.tester_next_step: raw RFC 3489 probe (no magic cookie); confirm plain MAPPED-ADDRESS

findings.title_pattern: STUN OTHER-ADDRESS discloses a second server IP
findings.promotion_notes: Rescan the disclosed second IP — the host was not in scope discovery.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -sU -p3478 <other-address-ip>  # portscan the second STUN interface

findings.title_pattern: STUN/TURN reflective amplification factor N x exceeds 4x
findings.tier_evidence: Amplification factor measured from real request/response byte lengths — objective probe result.
findings.promotion_notes: DDoS building block; recce cannot itself amplify.
findings.tester_next_step: n/a — DDoS proof would be unsafe; report the ratio only

findings.title_pattern: TURNS TLS posture is weak (protocol version or certificate)
findings.tier_evidence: TLS handshake result: version + cert self-signed.
Always emitted for a reachable endpoint.
